facts.text: MaxEventStreams is 8; a stream that pushes the open count past it is refused with a busy error.
Journal pages requested by DrainChangesAsync hold at most ChangePageSize rows, which is 200.
One stream tick may deliver at most ChangeDrainCap rows, which is 5000, before the client is told to reset.
DefaultRevisionPollInterval is 500 milliseconds and applies when the constructor receives no poll interval.
at: private static readonly TimeSpan DefaultRevisionPollInterval = TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(500);

facts.text: DefaultKeepaliveInterval is 5 seconds, the value KeepaliveInterval starts from for an idle event stream.
at: private static readonly TimeSpan DefaultKeepaliveInterval = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5);

facts.text: RetryFrame sends retry: 1000 so an EventSource client reconnects after one second.
at: private static readonly byte[] RetryFrame = Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes("retry: 1000\n\n");

facts.text: KeepaliveFrame is a comment line padded with 1024 spaces so an idle proxy does not close the stream.
The constructor always registers the 127.0.0.1 prefix for the serve port, so that address is served even when localhost is not.
When ShouldAddLocalhostPrefix returns false the constructor writes a warning to stderr and registers only 127.0.0.1.
Stop returns immediately on a second call because Interlocked.Exchange on stopped already returned 1.
Stop waits at most 5 seconds for the accept loop before it moves on to the handlers.
Stop gives running handlers 2 seconds through Task.WaitAll before it waits for the poller.
Loop starts each handler with Task.Run and records the task in handlers so Stop can wait for it.
A handler that throws writes a 500 JSON envelope with code internal and the exception message.
A Host header that fails IsLoopbackHost gets a 421 response with code invalid_host and message host not allowed.
Any method other than GET gets a 405 response with code read_only and message GET only.
A DossierRequestException maps to 404 for subject_not_found or fact_not_found and to 400 for every other code.
A FormatException raised while reading a query value is answered with 400 and code invalid_request.
The /api/search route parses limit with int.Parse, so a non-numeric limit falls through to the FormatException handler.

GET /api/compile serves text/markdown; charset=utf-8 when format equals markdown, and JSON otherwise.

facts.text: The need query parameter is read with query.GetValues so one request can pass several needs.
recency is parsed with double.Parse under InvariantCulture and becomes the Recency value of RankOptions.
GET /api/graph builds its request with GraphRequest.FromQuery from subject, depth, facts and max_nodes.
GET /api/fact without an id throws DossierRequestException with code invalid_request and message id is required.
Any path the switch does not match is answered with 404 and code not_found.
Write sets ContentLength64, adds Content-Security-Policy and X-Content-Type-Options nosniff, then closes the response.
Start reads the store revision once before listener.Start so a stream opened before the first poll has a baseline.
Stop waits at most 2 seconds for the poller task after the handlers.
Stop swallows an HttpListenerException from listener.Close when the port is still held, so Dispose does not throw.
A stream over the MaxEventStreams cap decrements openStreams before writing the busy response so the counter stays balanced.
The stream writes RetryFrame, then the revision frame, then drains the journal before its wait loop.
GET / is answered with IndexHtml under content type text/html; charset=utf-8.
GET /api/revision serializes a RevisionResponse built from the store's current revision.
GET /api/subjects answers with the result of Ops.Subjects for the store.

facts.text: The localhost prefix is added only when ShouldAddLocalhostPrefix returns true for the resolved addresses and CanBind.
GET /api/changes is served by ReadChangesPage from the since, limit and last query parameters.
The query helper Q returns null when a parameter is missing or empty, so an empty value never reaches a parser.

facts.text: CanBind proves an address usable by binding a throwaway socket to port 0 on that address.
When limit is absent ReadChangesPage asks the store for 100 journal rows.
When last is given ReadChangesPage returns store.ReadChangesLast and never applies limit.
A since value that is negative or unparseable is rejected as invalid_request with message since must be a non-negative integer.

facts.text: A limit that is not an integer is rejected as invalid_request with message limit must be an integer.
at: throw new DossierRequestException("invalid_request", "limit must be an integer");

facts.text: A stream refused by the cap gets 503 with code busy and a message naming MaxEventStreams.
The event stream sets ContentType text/event-stream, SendChunked and KeepAlive true, and Cache-Control no-store.
On an idle timeout the stream writes KeepaliveFrame and, when journalBehind is set, retries DrainChangesAsync.
The stream catches IO, listener, disposed, invalid-operation and socket errors and aborts the response instead of writing an error frame.
at: catch (Exception exception) when (exception is IOException or HttpListenerException or ObjectDisposedException or InvalidOperationException or SocketException)

facts.text: The wait between wakes uses KeepaliveInterval as its timeout, and a timeout is what triggers a keepalive write.
A journal read that throws returns the cursor unchanged with Behind true so the caller retries without ending the stream.
at: page = ChangesReader is { } reader ? reader(journal, ChangePageSize) : store.ReadChanges(journal, ChangePageSize);

facts.text: A page whose Reset flag is set writes one reset frame and returns the revision as the new cursor.
A page still Truncated after the tick drained ChangeDrainCap rows makes the stream write a reset instead of continuing.
An empty journal page returns the cursor with Behind false and writes no frame.
Each changes frame carries id equal to page.Next so a reconnect resumes after the delivered page.
The reset frame uses the revision string as both its id and its data.
ReadResumePoint prefers the Last-Event-ID header over the since query parameter.
A Last-Event-ID that is negative or unparseable falls through to the since parameter instead of being used.
at: if (long.TryParse(header, style, culture, out var resumed) && resumed >= 0)

facts.text: With neither Last-Event-ID nor since, the resume point is the revision the server last polled.
at: return long.TryParse(since, style, culture, out var fromQuery) && fromQuery >= 0 ? fromQuery : current;

facts.text: A revision read that throws ObjectDisposedException ends the poller, while any other exception skips the tick.
